next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State, Election Division

glance_notes.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Register to Vote
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for Indiana's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5, 2026. Online applications must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on the deadline, and mailed applications must be postmarked by the deadline.

glance_notes.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: Early In-Person Voting: Indiana provides no-excuse in-person absentee voting, commonly called early voting. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, it begins October 6 and continues through noon on November 2.

glance_notes.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: Absentee-by-Mail Requires a Qualifying Reason: Unlike in-person early voting, ordinary absentee voting by mail in Indiana is not available to every voter without a reason. A voter must meet at least one of the qualifying circumstances established by state law. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, an absentee-by-mail application must be received by 11:59 p.m. on October 22.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Indiana residents can register online through IndianaVoters.in.gov, by mail, in person through a county voter registration office, or through participating agencies such as the Bureau of Motor Vehicles. To vote in the November 3, 2026 General Election, you must be a U.S. citizen and Indiana resident, be at least 18 years old on or before the General Election, have lived in your precinct for at least 30 days before the election unless a legal exception applies, not currently be imprisoned following a criminal conviction, and be registered to vote. Online registration requires a valid Indiana driver's license or Indiana state-issued identification card.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, county office or participating agency
register.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: The Indiana Secretary of State directly establishes citizenship, Indiana residence, age, 30-day precinct residence, registration and criminal-conviction eligibility requirements. A person loses voting eligibility while imprisoned after conviction but is not permanently disenfranchised by the conviction. The official 2026 Indiana Voter Information Guide confirms the same requirements: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Indiana-Voter-Information-Guide.pdf](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Indiana-Voter-Information-Guide.pdf). IndianaVoters.in.gov is the state's official online registration and voter-information portal.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use IndianaVoters.in.gov to check your voter registration status. The official voter portal also allows voters to find their polling place, check provisional-ballot status, find county election contact information and see who will appear on their ballot for an upcoming election.
check_registration.internal_note: The Indiana Secretary of State registration page directly identifies IndianaVoters.in.gov as the official portal for validating registration status, finding polling places, checking provisional-ballot status, locating county contacts and determining who is on a voter's ballot. Supporting source: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/).

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The voter registration deadline for Indiana's November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5, 2026. Online voter registration applications must be submitted by 11:59 p.m. on October 5. Mailed voter registration applications must be postmarked on or before October 5. Indiana does not provide general Election Day voter registration, although special extended registration procedures exist for certain qualifying military voters and their family members.
deadlines.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — 2026 Indiana Voter Information Guide
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 voter guide directly establishes October 5, 2026 as the General Election registration deadline and specifies the postmark and 11:59 p.m. online rules. The registration page confirms the same date: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/). Certain military voters, spouses and dependents may qualify for extended registration procedures through noon on Election Day; those special procedures are addressed in military_overseas.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use IndianaVoters.in.gov to find the Election Day polling location associated with your voter registration. Some Indiana counties operate vote centers, which may allow eligible county voters to vote at any approved vote-center location rather than a single assigned precinct polling place. Check the official voter portal before Election Day for the location and voting options that apply to your address and county.
polling_place.internal_note: The Indiana Secretary of State registration page confirms that IndianaVoters.in.gov provides polling-place information. Indiana also authorizes county vote-center plans, so the reader-facing language avoids incorrectly implying that every Indiana voter is restricted to one traditional precinct polling location. Vote-center information is also available through the state's VoteCenters.IN.gov resources.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Indiana's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 6:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. local time. Voters casting a regular ballot in person generally must present identification meeting Indiana's photo ID requirements. A voter who cannot or does not present qualifying identification may cast a provisional ballot and has until noon 10 days after the election to provide the required documentation or establish that a legal exemption applies.
election_day.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — 2026 Indiana Voter Information Guide
election_day.internal_note: The 2026 voter guide confirms November 3 as General Election Day, describes the polls as open for 12 hours from 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., and establishes the photo-ID requirement. Current provisional-ballot guidance is available at [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/provisional-ballots/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/provisional-ballots/). Indiana spans Eastern and Central time zones, so local time is important.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Indiana polling places are open from 6:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. local time on Election Day. A voter who is in line at the polling place when voting ends at 6:00 p.m. is entitled to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — 2026 Indiana Voter Information Guide
polling_hours.internal_note: The official 2026 voter guide repeatedly identifies the Election Day voting period as 6:00 a.m.-6:00 p.m. Indiana counties are divided between Eastern and Central time zones, so the hours apply in local prevailing time.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Indiana provides no-excuse in-person absentee voting, commonly called early voting. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, in-person absentee voting begins October 6 and continues through noon local time on November 2. Every county must also provide in-person absentee voting on the two Saturdays immediately before Election Day. Exact locations, dates and daily hours vary by county, so voters should use IndianaVoters.in.gov or contact their county election office for local schedules.
early_voting.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State states that counties must make in-person absentee voting available for 28 days before an election, ending at noon local prevailing time on the day before Election Day, and must offer voting on the two Saturdays immediately before the election. The 2026 Indiana Voter Information Guide specifically identifies October 6 as the first day of General Election in-person absentee voting. County-specific locations and hours are published through IndianaVoters.in.gov.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Indiana requires most voters using ordinary absentee-by-mail voting to meet at least one qualifying reason established by state law. Qualifying circumstances include being absent from the county during all Election Day polling hours, having a disability, being at least 65 years old, having certain election duties, working during all polling hours, being confined by illness or injury or caring for someone who is confined, observing a qualifying religious discipline or holiday, participating in the state's address confidentiality program, being a member of the military or a public safety officer, qualifying under certain fail-safe voting procedures, being classified under state law as a serious sex offender, or lacking transportation to the polls. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the absentee-by-mail application must be received by 11:59 p.m. on October 22. An approved domestic absentee ballot must be received by 6:00 p.m. on Election Day.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Qualifying reason required; apply by October 22
absentee_mail.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The current Secretary of State absentee page directly lists the qualifying reasons. The official 2026 voter guide establishes October 22, 2026 as the General Election absentee-by-mail application deadline and the 6:00 p.m. Election Day ballot receipt deadline: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Indiana-Voter-Information-Guide.pdf](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Indiana-Voter-Information-Guide.pdf). Beginning July 1, 2023, absentee applications also require either a qualifying photo-ID copy or one or more specified voter identification numbers. Military and overseas voters have separate return rules documented in military_overseas.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Indiana generally requires a voter casting a ballot in person to present photo identification. The identification must display the voter's photo, contain a name that conforms to the voter registration record, contain an expiration date and either be current or have expired after the most recent General Election, and be issued by the State of Indiana, the U.S. government, or a federally recognized Native American Indian tribe or band. Certain military and tribal identification without an expiration date may qualify. Common acceptable documents include an Indiana driver's license, Indiana photo identification card, U.S. military identification or U.S. passport. Effective July 1, 2025, identification issued by an educational institution cannot be used as voter photo identification. A voter without qualifying identification may cast a provisional ballot and later satisfy the identification requirement or establish a legal exemption.
voter_id.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Photo ID Law
voter_id.internal_note: The current Secretary of State guidance establishes the photo, name, expiration and issuing-authority requirements and specifically notes the July 1, 2025 change prohibiting educational-institution identification. The 2026 Indiana Voter Information Guide independently confirms the current requirements. Absentee-by-mail and traveling-board voters do not present photo identification at a polling place, although identification information is required with absentee applications.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Indiana requires polling locations and voting systems to be accessible to voters with disabilities. At least one accessible voting machine must be available at each polling place. A voter who needs assistance may choose someone to help, except the voter's employer or union officer, or may receive assistance from poll workers representing the major political parties. Indiana also offers traveling-board absentee voting for certain voters who are confined or have disabilities, and voters with qualifying print disabilities may use a specialized absentee process that can provide an accessible electronic ballot compatible with screen-reader technology.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment and voting assistance available
accessible_voting.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Election Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State states that HAVA requires at least one accessible voting machine at each polling place and that polling facilities must be physically accessible. The 2026 voter guide confirms voter-assistance rights. The absentee page, [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/absentee-voting/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/absentee-voting/), describes traveling-board voting and the ABS-VPD process for voters with print disabilities, including accessible electronic ballots through OmniBallot.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Indiana provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible military and overseas voters. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot. Depending on the voter's circumstances and chosen delivery method, ballots may be transmitted and returned by mail, email or fax. For qualifying military and overseas ballots returned by mail, the ballot must be postmarked by Election Day and received by the circuit court clerk no later than noon 10 days after the election. Certain military voters and qualifying spouses or dependents may also be eligible for extended voter registration procedures.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA plus special delivery and return options
military_overseas.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The official 2026 Military and Overseas Voters Guide confirms FPCA use and mail, email and fax ballot options: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Military-and-Overseas-Voters-Guide.pdf](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Military-and-Overseas-Voters-Guide.pdf). It states that ballots returned by mail must be postmarked by Election Day and received no later than noon 10 days after the election. Indiana also provides extended registration in certain circumstances for military voters and their spouses or dependents, potentially through noon on Election Day. UOCAVA procedures should not be confused with ordinary domestic absentee-by-mail rules.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: Indiana college students may choose to register at the address where they live while attending school or at the address where they live when they are not attending school, provided they otherwise meet Indiana's voter qualifications. A student may register at only one residence. Indiana law does not allow a voter's eligibility to be challenged solely because the voter attends an educational institution or because the registration address is student housing. Effective July 1, 2025, an identification document issued by an educational institution cannot be used to satisfy Indiana's voter photo-ID requirement.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may choose one qualifying voting residence
student_voting.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — 2026 Voter Registration Guidebook
student_voting.internal_note: The official 2026 Voter Registration Guidebook specifically states that college students may register either where they live while attending school or where they live while not attending school and may register at only one of those locations. It also states that enrollment or student housing cannot by itself form the basis of a voter challenge. Current student-ID restriction is independently confirmed by the Secretary of State Photo ID Law page: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/photo-id-law/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/photo-id-law/).

sample_ballot.label: Official Ballot Information
sample_ballot.content: Indiana voters can use IndianaVoters.in.gov and its Who's on My Ballot feature to review the candidates and ballot information associated with their registration for an upcoming election. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's address and districts, voters should use the personalized state voter portal rather than relying on a generic statewide ballot.
sample_ballot.source_name: Indiana Statewide Voter Portal — Who's on My Ballot
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Indiana Secretary of State registration page expressly states that IndianaVoters.in.gov allows voters to determine Who's on My Ballot for an upcoming election: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/). The Election Division also publishes the official 2026 General Election candidate list, but the personalized voter portal is the more useful reader-facing resource because local and district contests vary by address.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Indiana Election Division, 302 West Washington Street, Room E-204, Indianapolis, IN 46204. Phone: 317-232-3939. Fax: 317-233-6793. Email: elections@iec.in.gov. Hoosier Voter Hotline: 866-IN-1-VOTE (866-461-8683). The Election Division is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. For questions about an individual voter registration record, local early-voting schedule, polling location or absentee ballot, voters may also contact their county election officials.
contact.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State — Indiana Election Division
contact.internal_note: The current Indiana Election Division staff page directly verifies the office address, 317-232-3939 front-desk number, 317-233-6793 fax, [elections@iec.in.gov](mailto:elections@iec.in.gov) email and Hoosier Voter Hotline. The Election Division homepage confirms Monday-Friday 8:00 a.m.-5:00 p.m. hours: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/). The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Indiana Secretary of State Election Division website for statewide election rules, voter guides, registration information, photo-ID requirements, absentee voting and military and overseas voting. IndianaVoters.in.gov is the state's voter portal for registration, registration-status checks, polling-place information, county contacts, provisional-ballot status and personalized ballot information. County election officials administer many local election functions, including early-voting locations and absentee-ballot processing.
official_resources.source_name: Indiana Secretary of State, Election Division
official_resources.internal_note: Official voter portal: [https://indianavoters.in.gov/](https://indianavoters.in.gov/). Official 2026 voter guide: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Indiana-Voter-Information-Guide.pdf](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/files/2026-Indiana-Voter-Information-Guide.pdf). Official registration information: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/register-to-vote/). Official absentee information: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/absentee-voting/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/absentee-voting/). Official photo-ID guidance: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/photo-id-law/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/photo-id-law/). Official military and overseas information: [https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/military-and-overseas-voters/](https://www.in.gov/sos/elections/voter-information/ways-to-vote/military-and-overseas-voters/). All source_url fields contain bare URL strings, and all reader-facing content uses plain text with no Markdown hyperlink syntax.
